propositions.text: The appellant is a Tunisian citizen appealing the RPD's rejection of his refugee claim under IRPA sections 96 and 97.
propositions.quote: The appellant, XXXX XXXX, a citizen of Tunisia, is appealing against the decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD), which rejected his claim for refugee protection by finding that he is neither a "Convention refugee" nor a "person in need of protection" within the meaning of sections 96 and 97 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The appellant, a Tunisian citizen, appeals the RPD's rejection of his refugee claim under IRPA sections 96 and 97, says the court.

propositions.text: Appellant's counsel asks RAD to allow appeal, set aside RPD decision, find appellant needs protection or refer for re-determination by different member.
propositions.quote: In the memorandum of appeal, counsel for the appellant is asking the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) to allow the appeal, set aside the RPD determination, determine that the appellant is a person in need of protection or refer the matter to the RPD for re-determination of the refugee protection claim by a different member.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant's counsel asks RAD to allow appeal, set aside RPD decision, or refer for re-determination, says appellant.

propositions.text: No new evidence was submitted with the appellant's record for this appeal.
propositions.quote: In this context, I find that no new evidence was submitted in support of this appeal.

propositions.text: Memorandum claims evidence was presented per subsection 110(4) IRPA for this appeal.
propositions.quote: The memorandum indicates that [translation] "evidence was presented in accordance with the requirements of subsection 110(4) of the IRPA for this appeal,"

paragraphs.summary: Applicant claims evidence was presented per IRPA 110(4), but court finds no new evidence submitted for this appeal.

propositions.text: Appellant requests a hearing and interpreter services for spouse's testimony.
propositions.quote: In the memorandum, the appellant is requesting that a hearing be held and requires the services of an interpreter so that his spouse can testify.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant requests hearing and interpreter for spouse's testimony, says appellant.

propositions.text: RAD confirms RPD's determination that appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection under IRPA.
propositions.quote: Pursuant to subsection 111(1) of the IRPA, the RAD confirms the determination of the RPD, namely, that XXXX XXXX is neither a "Convention refugee" under section 96 of the IRPA nor a "person in need of protection" under section 97 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: RAD confirms RPD's determination that appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor person in need of protection, says court.

propositions.text: The appeal is dismissed.
propositions.quote: The appeal is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The appeal is dismissed, says court.

propositions.text: Claimant is Tunisian Muslim who came to Canada in 2014 and claimed refugee protection in 2015 due to fear from marrying a Catholic woman and attending Catholic churches.
propositions.quote: The refugee protection claimant is a citizen of Tunisia and a Muslim. He came to Canada as a visitor on XXXX XXXX, 2014. He made a refugee protection claim on May 4, 2015. He alleges a well-founded fear of persecution and a risk to his life by reason of his marriage to a Catholic woman in XXXX 2015 and his attending Catholic churches.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant is Tunisian Muslim who fears persecution due to marriage to Catholic woman and church attendance, says court.

propositions.text: In BOC Form, claimant alleges dating a Catholic woman, agreed to convert to Christianity to marry, and family was informed.
propositions.quote: In his Basis of Claim Form (BOC Form), he alleges that he began dating an XXXX woman of the Catholic faith. He agreed to convert to Christianity in order to marry his wife. The claimant's parents were informed of his marriage and that he was going to church in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant alleges dating Catholic woman, agreed to convert, and family was informed, says court.

propositions.text: Claimant's family considers him a shame and alleges death awaits converts in Tunisia.
propositions.quote: His family in Tunisia considers him a shame on the family. He alleges that, in Tunisia, death awaits anyone who changes religion.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant's family shames him and death allegedly awaits converts in Tunisia, says court.

propositions.text: RPD found claimant not credible and testimony untrustworthy on central claim elements due to omissions, inconsistencies, and implausibilities.
propositions.quote: On July 27, 2015, the RPD rejected the refugee protection claim, finding that [translation] "the claimant was not credible and his testimony was not trustworthy with regard to the central elements of the claim." The RPD noted several omissions in the BOC Form, and inconsistencies and implausibilities in the evidence.

propositions.text: RPD believes claimant did not convert to Catholicism nor intend to do so.
propositions.quote: In short, the RPD [translation] "believes that the claimant did not convert to Catholicism and did not demonstrate that he intended to do so."

propositions.text: RPD drew negative inference from claimant's failure to corroborate willingness to convert.
propositions.quote: In addition, the panel draws a negative inference from the claimant's lack of effort to corroborate his testimony on his willingness to convert to Catholicism.

paragraphs.summary: RPD found claimant not credible, disbelieved conversion, and drew negative inference from lack of corroboration, says earlier decision-maker.

propositions.text: RPD found no prohibition on Muslim-Christian marriage and no systematic persecution of such couples in Tunisia.
propositions.quote: The RPD noted that the documentary evidence indicates that there is nothing prohibiting Muslims from marrying non-Muslims, and that there are many mixed couples in Tunisia. According to the RPD, the evidence does not allow for the conclusion that Muslims married to Christians are systematically persecuted in Tunisia.

paragraphs.summary: RPD found no prohibition or systematic persecution of Muslim-Christian marriages in Tunisia, says earlier decision-maker.

propositions.text: Appellant submits RPD erred by rejecting his refugee protection claim.
propositions.quote: The appellant submits that the RPD erred by rejecting his refugee protection claim.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant submits RPD erred in rejecting his refugee claim, says appellant.

propositions.text: Appellant relies on Maldonado that sworn testimony is presumed true unless valid reason to doubt.
propositions.quote: The appellant is relying on Maldonado5 and submits that sworn testimony is presumed to be true, unless there is a valid reason to doubt its truthfulness.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant relies on Maldonado that sworn testimony is presumed true absent valid doubt, says appellant.

propositions.text: Appellant cites Giron cautioning against adverse findings on implausibilities due to cultural differences.
propositions.quote: He also cited the Federal Court of Appeal decision in Giron,6 which advises caution when making adverse findings based on implausibilities because refugee protection claimants come from diverse cultures and "actions which might appear implausible if judged by Canadian standards might be plausible when considered within the context of the claimant's social and cultural background."

paragraphs.summary: Appellant cites Giron cautioning on adverse findings from implausibilities due to cultural context, says appellant.

propositions.text: Claimant invokes IRPA 110(6) to be heard before RAD and call wife as witness.
propositions.quote: The claimant is invoking the provisions of subsection 110(6) of the IRPA, and is asking to be heard before the RAD and to call his wife as a witness.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant invokes IRPA 110(6) to be heard and call wife as witness, says claimant.

propositions.text: Singh says RAD proceeds without hearing except where documentary evidence raises serious credibility issue central to claim and could justify allowing or rejecting claim.
propositions.quote: In Singh,7 the Federal Court of Appeal reiterated the principle that the RAD proceed without holding a hearing. According to the Court, this principle "is subject to an exception only where the documentary evidence '(a) [...] raises a serious issue with respect to the credibility of the person who is the subject of the appeal; (b) [...] is central to the decision with respect to the refugee protection claim; and (c) [...] if accepted, would justify allowing or rejecting the refugee protection claim.'"

paragraphs.summary: Singh says RAD proceeds without hearing except if documentary evidence raises serious credibility issue central to claim, says prior court.

propositions.text: Appellant submitted no new evidence; therefore RAD cannot hold a hearing.
propositions.quote: In this case, the appellant submitted no new evidence in support of his appeal. Therefore, the RAD cannot hold a hearing.

paragraphs.summary: No new evidence was submitted; thus RAD cannot hold a hearing, says court.

propositions.text: Huruglica ruled on RAD's reasonableness standard when credibility not at issue.
propositions.quote: In Huruglica,8 the Federal Court of Appeal ruled on the issue of whether it was reasonable for the RAD, when credibility was not an issue, to examine the findings of fact, mixed fact and law by using the reasonableness standard.

paragraphs.summary: Huruglica ruled on RAD's reasonableness standard when credibility not at issue, says prior court.

propositions.text: Justice Gauthier notes RAD is safety net catching RPD mistakes on law or facts.
propositions.quote: Interpreting the statutory provisions and making a passing reference to Parliament's intention in implementing the RAD, Justice Gauthier notes: [98] The RAD was essentially viewed as the safety net that would catch all mistakes made by the RPD, be it on the law or the facts.

paragraphs.summary: Justice Gauthier notes RAD is safety net catching RPD mistakes on law or facts, says prior court.

propositions.text: Parliament intended RAD to correct RPD errors of law, fact or mixed fact and law under standard of correctness.
propositions.quote: Parliament's intention must be determined by referring first to the statute, specifically to sections 110 and 111 of the IRPA, about which the Court of Appeal indicates: [59] ... Paragraph 111(2)(a) does not distinguish between errors of law, fact or mixed fact and law. It simply requires that the decision of the RPD be "wrong in law, in fact or in mixed fact and law" (in French: "erronée en droit, en fait ou en droit et en fait"). [64] The ordinary meaning of the word "wrong" is "not correct or true", "incorrect", "mistaken": The Oxford English Dictionary, 3d ed., s.v. "wrong". The French version "erronée" has the exact same ordinary meaning, that is, "fausse", "incorrecte", "inexacte", "mal fondée": Le nouveau petit Robert, 2006, s.v. "erroné". This wording definitively points to the standard of correctness. In addition, the legislator's intent to use the word "wrong" in its ordinary meaning is, in my view, supported by the legislative history, to which I will refer later.

paragraphs.summary: Parliament intended RAD to correct RPD errors of law, fact or mixed fact and law under correctness standard, says prior court.

propositions.text: RPD may have advantage over RAD in assessing credibility or weight of oral evidence
propositions.quote: ...that there may be cases where the RPD enjoys a meaningful advantage over the RAD in making findings of fact or mixed fact and law, because they require an assessment of the credibility or weight to be given to the oral evidence it hears.

propositions.text: RAD should exercise restraint before substituting its own determination, decided case-by-case
propositions.quote: ...the RAD should sometimes exercise a degree of restraint before substituting its own determination, the issue of whether the circumstances warrant such restraint ought to be addressed on a case-by-case basis.

propositions.text: RAD must determine if RPD had advantage and if it can still make final decision on refugee claim
propositions.quote: In each case, the RAD ought to determine whether the RPD truly benefited from an advantageous position, and if so, whether the RAD can nevertheless make a final decision in respect of the refugee claim.

paragraphs.summary: The Court states RPD may have advantage in credibility findings; RAD should exercise restraint case-by-case but decide if it can make final decision.

propositions.text: RAD's role is to intervene if RPD is wrong in law, fact, or mixed fact and law applying correctness standard
propositions.quote: ...the role of the RAD is to intervene when the RPD is wrong in law, in fact or in fact and law. This translates into an application of the correctness standard of review.

propositions.text: If error found, RAD can confirm, set aside, or substitute decision unless it needs to hear RPD evidence
propositions.quote: If there is an error, the RAD can still confirm the decision of the RPD on another basis. It can also set it aside, substituting its own determination of the claim, unless it is satisfied that it cannot do either without hearing the evidence presented to the RPD

paragraphs.summary: Court of Appeal says RAD intervenes if RPD erred, applying correctness standard, and can substitute decision unless it must hear RPD evidence.

propositions.text: RAD reviews RPD findings of fact and mixed fact and law with no credibility issue applying correctness standard
propositions.quote: ...with respect to findings of fact (and mixed fact and law) such as the one involved here, which raised no issue of credibility of oral evidence, the RAD is to review RPD decisions applying the correctness standard.

propositions.text: RAD must analyze record independently and confirm or set aside RPD decision
propositions.quote: ...the RAD carries out its own analysis of the record to determine whether, as submitted by the appellant, the RPD erred. Having done this, the RAD is to provide a final determination, either by confirming the RPD decision or setting it aside and substituting its own determination

propositions.text: RAD refers matter back to RPD only if it cannot decide without hearing RPD oral evidence
propositions.quote: It is only when the RAD is of the opinion that it cannot provide such a final determination without hearing the oral evidence presented to the RPD that the matter can be referred back to the RPD for redetermination.

paragraphs.summary: Justice Gauthier holds RAD reviews RPD findings without credibility issues on correctness standard and decides or refers back if needed.

propositions.text: I will independently analyze evidence to determine correctness of RPD decision and intervene if error found
propositions.quote: I will conduct an independent analysis of the evidence in order to formulate my own opinion on this refugee protection claim and to determine whether the decision rendered is correct. If an error of fact, of law or of mixed fact and law has been made, I will intervene

paragraphs.summary: I will independently analyze evidence and intervene if RPD decision is incorrect, as per Court of Appeal guidance.

propositions.text: RPD found appellant's credibility was the determinative issue
propositions.quote: Before the RPD, the determinative issue was the appellant's credibility.

propositions.text: RPD has advantage over RAD in credibility assessments due to hearing witnesses
propositions.quote: Generally, the RPD is in a more privileged position than the RAD because it has the advantage of seeing and hearing the refugee protection claimants and witnesses.

propositions.text: RAD will not have hearing privilege but must independently assess evidence and intervene if error found
propositions.quote: In this case, the RAD will not have this privilege because it will not hold a hearing. However, I must conduct an independent assessment of the evidence to determine whether the decision rendered is correct. If an error of fact, of law or of mixed fact and law has been made, I will have to intervene

paragraphs.summary: RPD found credibility key; RPD has hearing advantage but RAD must independently assess evidence and intervene if error found.

propositions.text: I reviewed all evidence to form my opinion on refugee claim
propositions.quote: I reviewed all the evidence in order to formulate my own opinion on this refugee protection claim.

propositions.text: Appellant's memorandum poorly explains RPD errors
propositions.quote: the appellant's memorandum is not very eloquent regarding the errors made by the RPD in the assessment of his refugee protection claim.

propositions.text: I find RPD rendered correct decision after considering arguments and evidence
propositions.quote: it is my opinion that the RPD rendered the correct decision. My reasons are as follows.

paragraphs.summary: I reviewed evidence; appellant poorly argued RPD errors; I find RPD decision correct.

propositions.text: Presumption of truthfulness can be rebutted by claimant's lack of credibility
propositions.quote: The presumption of truthfulness mentioned in Maldonado is not unchallengeable and a claimant's lack of credibility is sufficient to rebut it.

propositions.text: Accumulated contradictions or omissions can justify negative credibility findings
propositions.quote: although some evidence may not be sufficient when taken individually, the accumulation of contradictions or omissions may serve as a basis for a negative credibility finding

propositions.text: This case involves accumulated contradictions and omissions undermining credibility
propositions.quote: which is true in this case.

paragraphs.summary: Maldonado presumption can be rebutted by lack of credibility; accumulated contradictions justify negative findings here.

propositions.text: RPD found appellant's credibility undermined by omissions in BOC Form of key claim elements
propositions.quote: One factor that the RPD found undermined the appellant's credibility was the omission in the BOC Form of several elements central to his refugee protection claim.

propositions.text: Appellant testified his brother and cousin threatened to torture him for marrying a Catholic and attending church in 2015
propositions.quote: the appellant testified that, in XXXX 2015, his brother and his cousin had threatened to torture him because he had married a Catholic and was attending a Catholic church.

propositions.text: Appellant did not mention these threats in BOC Form
propositions.quote: However, the claimant did not mention these threats in his BOC Form.

propositions.text: RPD deemed appellant's explanation for omission insufficient
propositions.quote: His explanation that he had put general information in his BOC Form without providing details was deemed insufficient by the RPD.

paragraphs.summary: RPD found appellant's credibility undermined by omissions of threats in BOC Form and rejected his explanation.

propositions.text: Appellant argues RPD erred in drawing negative inference from omission, saying fear implied threats
propositions.quote: The appellant argued that the RPD erred in drawing a negative inference from that omission. He stated that he "testified in his written form that he feared his family, implying that they had threatened him

propositions.text: I cannot accept appellant's argument
propositions.quote: With due respect for the argument presented, I cannot accept it.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant argues omission inference was error; I reject this argument.

propositions.text: Board can base negative credibility findings on omissions and inconsistencies in entry notes, PIF, and oral testimony
propositions.quote: A long line of case law has established that the Board can base its negative credibility findings on the omissions and inconsistencies that it notes regarding the important facts alleged in the notes taken at the point of entry, in the Personal Information Form and in the oral testimony.

paragraphs.summary: Case law allows Board to base negative credibility findings on omissions and inconsistencies in key documents and testimony.

propositions.text: RPD justified in drawing negative inference from claimant's failure to detail threats in BOC Form
propositions.quote: The RPD was justified in drawing a negative inference from the fact that the claimant failed to mention those threats in the BOC Form and to give some details.

propositions.text: BOC Form question 2(a) requires detailed explanation of what happened and when
propositions.quote: question 2(a) of the BOC Form requires claimants to explain in detail what happened to them and when.

propositions.text: Claimant also failed to mention cousin's toughness and membership in a Tunisian group relevant to threats
propositions.quote: the appellant failed to indicate in the BOC Form that his cousin is a tough man, that he is a member of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX an XXXXgroupXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX in Tunisia.

propositions.text: RPD noted these facts are not trivial as they relate to basis of fear
propositions.quote: As the RPD noted, these are not trivial facts; they relate to the threats that form the basis of his fear.

paragraphs.summary: RPD justified in negative inference from claimant's failure to detail threats and relevant facts in BOC Form.

propositions.text: RPD drew negative inference from claimant's omission in BOC Form about family marginalization for not following Islam
propositions.quote: The RPD drew a negative inference from the fact that the claimant also failed to indicate in the BOC Form that his family marginalized him in Tunisia because he did not follow the precepts of Islam; he drank alcohol, did not go to the mosque regularly and did not observe Ramadan in XXXX.

propositions.text: Claimant stated in BOC Form he had no religious problems in Tunisia, contradicting testimony
propositions.quote: the claimant stated in the BOC Form that he did not have any problems in Tunisia due to his religion.

propositions.text: Omission undermined credibility
propositions.quote: The omission of these aspects in the BOC Form, about which he testified, undermined his credibility

paragraphs.summary: RPD found claimant's omission about family marginalization and contradictory BOC Form statement undermined credibility.

propositions.text: RPD noted contradiction between BOC Form and hearing about church attendance with wife
propositions.quote: The RPD noted a contradiction that I find important. The claimant stated in the BOC Form that he attended XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX church with his wife. Yet, at the hearing, he stated that he went without her.

propositions.text: This contradiction is not trivial and supports serious doubt about church attendance
propositions.quote: This is not a trivial contradiction and tends to support serious doubt when he states he attends a Christian church.

paragraphs.summary: RPD found contradiction about church attendance with wife; I find it supports serious doubt.

propositions.text: Claimant contradicted himself about frequency and language of mass attendance
propositions.quote: The appellant also contradicted himself about how frequently he attended mass and the language in which it was celebrated.

propositions.text: Claimant initially said mass was four or five times and in XXXX; then changed to attending two churches after confrontation
propositions.quote: At the hearing, he stated first that he attended mass four or five times on XXXX XXXXnd that the mass was in XXXX. When confronted... the claimant changed his testimony and answered that he attended two churches.

propositions.text: Contradictions are not trivial and support serious doubt about church attendance
propositions.quote: Again, the facts are not trivial; his attending a Christian church is at the heart of his problems. The contradictions in his testimony tend to support serious doubt.

paragraphs.summary: Claimant contradicted himself on mass attendance frequency and language; contradictions support serious doubt.

propositions.text: RPD found claimant did not take or register for catechism classes and could not name sacraments
propositions.quote: the claimant did not take catechism classes and did not register for catechism classes. He is unable to name one of the sacraments of the Catholic religion.

propositions.text: Claimant claimed to have consulted parish priest about baptism but did not know priest's name
propositions.quote: he claims to have consulted the parish priest about a possible baptism and, furthermore, he did not know the name of the priest with whom he had discussed this.

propositions.text: These factors support RPD's disbelief of claimant's conversion to Catholicism
propositions.quote: In the credibility assessment... the RPD also considered the following factors...

paragraphs.summary: RPD found claimant's lack of catechism, knowledge, and priest's name undermined conversion claim.

propositions.text: Testimony alone cannot be discredited for lack of corroboration
propositions.quote: A claimant's testimony cannot be discredited simply because it is not corroborated by the documentary evidence.

propositions.text: Board may consider absence of corroboration when corroboration would be expected
propositions.quote: the Board may take account of the absence of corroborative evidence in circumstances where one would expect it to exist.

propositions.text: RPD had serious doubts about claimant's statements due to accumulation of problems
propositions.quote: the RPD, due to an accumulation of problems related to the claimant's statements, had serious doubts about his allegations.

propositions.text: RPD drew negative inference from appellant's wife not corroborating by testimony or affidavit
propositions.quote: it was justified in this context to draw a negative inference from the fact that the appellant's wife did not corroborate the claimant's testimony either by testifying directly or by submitting an affidavit.

propositions.text: RPD noted appellant's lack of effort to obtain wife's affidavit undermined credibility
propositions.quote: the RPD noted that the appellant's lack of effort to obtain an affidavit from his wife undermined his credibility.

propositions.text: I agree RPD was justified to consider lack of wife's corroboration as undermining credibility
propositions.quote: In my opinion, it was an element that the RPD could have expected and, in the context of this case, the RPD was justified to consider that element.

paragraphs.summary: Testimony need not be corroborated but RPD reasonably doubted claimant and negatively inferred from wife's lack of corroboration.

propositions.text: RPD drew negative inference from implausibility that conservative Catholic family allowed daughter to marry Muslim before conversion
propositions.quote: The RPD drew a negative inference from the implausibility that a conservative Catholic family had allowed their daughter to marry a Muslim man before he converted, when it was a condition of their accepting the union.

paragraphs.summary: RPD negatively inferred from implausibility of conservative Catholic family allowing daughter to marry Muslim before conversion.

propositions.text: Credibility findings based on implausibility require clearest cases
propositions.quote: In Subramaniyathas, the Federal Court states: "In contrast to credibility findings based on inconsistencies, contradictions or evasions, credibility findings based on implausibility may only be made in the clearest of cases."

propositions.text: I consider implausibility finding not determinative here
propositions.quote: I am of the opinion that this finding is not determinative in this case.

paragraphs.summary: Federal Court requires clearest cases for implausibility findings; I find implausibility here not determinative.

propositions.text: RPD noted claimant said he renounced Islam but still presents as Muslim, which is curious
propositions.quote: As noted by the RPD, it is curious that the refugee protection claimant stated that he had renounced Islam but that he still presents himself as Muslim.

paragraphs.summary: RPD found it curious claimant renounced Islam but still presents as Muslim.

propositions.text: I conclude RPD rendered correct decision; appellant did not show error in fact, law, or mixed fact and law
propositions.quote: it is my opinion that the RPD rendered the correct decision in this case; the appellant did not establish that the decision is not based on the evidence or that the RPD committed an error in fact, in law or in mixed fact and law.

propositions.text: Given evidence, I would have rendered same decision
propositions.quote: In light of the evidence in the record, I would have rendered the same decision.

paragraphs.summary: I conclude RPD decision is correct and I would have made the same decision based on evidence.

propositions.text: Confirm the RPD's determination that the appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97
propositions.quote: I confirm the determination of the RPD, namely, that XXXX XXXX is neither a "Convention refugee" under section 96 of the IRPA nor a "person in need of protection" under section 97 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The court confirms the RPD's decision that the appellant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection under IRPA sections 96 and 97.

propositions.text: Dismiss the appeal
propositions.quote: The appeal is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The court dismisses the appeal.
